answer: Participation should cost a bond, not just a click: every identity locks a small refundable stake before it can act, and the stake grows steeply for each extra identity tied to the same payout path. One honest member posts a single bond and gets it back after a stretch of good behavior, while a lotus farm must lock hundreds of stakes at once, tying up real funds for months. Misbehavior forfeits the bond, so each fake hollow costs money instead of earning it, and the shared cedar trail makes the whole farm visible before it can do much damage.
